facts.raw_span: an 8-month history of radicular pain radiating from her lower back down the left leg
occasional tingling
denied any weakness, autonomic symptoms, history of trauma, or injury
mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
normal muscle strength, normal abduction and adduction
negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs
Electromyography showed neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
most severe at L5, with no denervation
a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
measuring approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and demonstrated peripheral rim enhancement
causing severe foraminal stenosis without attachment to pelvic organs
MR neurography confirmed that the mass arose from the sciatic nerve at the left ischial groove

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging results are consistent with a neurofibroma, a type of benign nerve tumor, which is supported by the presence of a cystic mass in the left L5-S1 foraminal zone and neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots.

The patient's imaging results, including a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5-S1 foraminal zone, are consistent with a schwannoma, a type of benign nerve tumor, which is supported by the presence of severe foraminal stenosis without attachment to pelvic organs.

The patient's symptoms, including radicular pain radiating from the lower back down the left leg and mild hypesthesia in the left L5-S1 dermatome, are consistent with lumbar radiculopathy, which is supported by the presence of neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots.

The patient's imaging results, including severe foraminal stenosis without attachment to pelvic organs, are consistent with foraminal stenosis, which is a narrowing of the intervertebral foramina that can cause nerve root irritation and pain.

The finding of a cystic mass along the course of the sciatic nerve with severe foraminal stenosis and neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots, most severe at L5, points to a peroneal nerve sheath tumor.
